ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier) Articles L561-1 to L561-59 and R561-1 et seq., as amended by Ordinance No. 2020-115 of 12 February 2020 and Decree No. 2020-118 of 12 February 2020 (transposing EU Directive (EU) 2018/843, 5th AMLD); Article L123-1 et seq. of the Commercial Code (corporate identification); Beneficial Ownership Register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs - RBE) under Articles L561-45 to L561-46 and R561-55 et seq. CMF, consolidated with the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS) and operated via the INPI Guichet unique; Tracfin reporting obligations under Article L561-15 CMF; GAFI/FATF recommendations and French DGT sanctions enforcement rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority, notary or competent certifying authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Hague Convention) for Convention signatories; otherwise Consular Legalization by French Embassy/Consulate of the issuing country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificat d'existence légale / non-faillite) of each foreign corporate founder, where applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or commercial court of the foreign UBO's state of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Convention signatories; otherwise Consular Legalization before the French consular post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate / extract of judicial record (extrait de casier judiciaire) of the designated gérant, issued within 3 months of filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice / national police authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Convention signatories; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address dated within 3 months (utility bill or bank statement) for the gérant and each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company or credit institution of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Convention signatories; otherwise Consular Legalization (banks and notaries may accept under internal compliance policies)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial ownership registration certificate from the home jurisdiction of each foreign corporate UBO (where such register exists)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign beneficial-ownership register or corporate registry of the respective jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Convention signatories; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for the planned French corporate bank account opening (Swift TT / Wire Transfer rails)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank where the founder / UBO maintains the primary account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Convention signatories; otherwise Consular Legalization (may be waived subject to the receiving French bank's internal AML acceptance decision)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under CMF Articles L561-4 to L561-7: identification and verification of all UBOs and directors, PEP status screening per Article L561-10 CMF, adverse media and enforcement list screening (OFAC SDN, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, French DGT/MEF sanctions files and Tracfin guidelines), verification of non-disqualification of the gérant under Commercial Code Articles L653-1 et seq., and FATF country risk rating assessment; negative screening is a pre-incorporation condition precedent.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI (Institut national de la propriété industrielle) at https://procedures.inpi.fr, with name availability pre-check via INPI Data (data.inpi.fr) and the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name of the SARL must be expressed in French or, if a foreign term is used, in Latin-alphabet characters and must not be contrary to public order, morality or established usage (Code de commerce, Articles R123-17 and R123-18). Non-Latin script names require transliteration into Latin characters. The name must be materially distinguishable from existing names in the RNCS, from protected French and EU trademarks (Code de la propriété intellectuelle, Article L711-4), and must not be deceptive regarding the company's object (matcha powder wholesale and distribution).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Legal form terms: 'SA', 'SAS', 'SNC', 'SCI' or any form inconsistent with the elected SARL structure
Official-state and public authority terms: 'République', 'France' (without ministerial authorization), 'National', 'Gouvernement', 'Ministère', 'Président', 'Préfet', 'État', 'Monnaie'

Regulated financial and professional terms requiring prior ministerial or professional-body approval: 'Banque', 'Assurance', 'Mutuelle', 'Caution', 'Pharmacien', 'Avocat', 'Notaire', 'Huissier', 'Expert-Comptable', 'Commissaire aux comptes'

Terms implying organic certification in the name (e.g., 'Bio', 'Organic', 'AB') where the matcha does not yet hold current EU organic certification under Regulation (EU) 2018/848 and the French AB/INAO framework
Terms contrary to public order, morality or deliberately misleading about business purpose (Crossref Code de commerce, Article L123-37)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a formal name pre-reservation regime; name availability is assessed at filing through the Guichet unique and the RCS. If the registry rejects the name (refusal of immatriculation or INPI incompatibility finding), the founders may: (1) re-file a corrected creation dossier on the Guichet unique without penalty within 8 days of the rejection notification; (2) file an administrative remedy (recours gracieux) with INPI within 30 days of rejection; (3) petition the President of the Tribunal judiciaire or the competent Commercial Court (currently the Comité de règlement amiable / the judiciary of the Tribunal de commerce) in accordance with Commercial Code Articles R123-139 et seq. within one month of the notification; and (4) contest trademark-conflict refusals before the INPI or the Paris Judicial Court under Article L716-4 of the Intellectual Property Code. Legal counsel should be engaged before re-filing if the rejection is based on trademark or public-interest grounds.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible: a French SARL must have a siège social located in the national territory. Commercial domiciliation with a licensed domiciliation company is expressly allowed under Commercial Code Articles R123-167 to R123-173, subject to: (a) prior declaration to the Préfet of the registered office department; (b) genuine physical access to the premises and a demonstrable substance link; (c) the arrangement limited to 2 months following commencement of operations unless extended under the 5-year renewal regime (Art. R123-170); (d) the domiciliation provider being prefecturally approved if it hosts more than 100 companies. For a low-risk wholesale matcha importer, a virtual office is acceptable in principle, but the DGFiP (French tax administration) may apply substance-over-form scrutiny in a tax audit if no business assets or employees are evidenced in France.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5% cumulative probability within the first 3 financial years for a low-risk wholesale matcha importer using a licensed domiciliation address; probability rises to approximately 20% where foreign non-EU UBOs are present or where the registered office is a micro-domiciliation provider without any French operational substance).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut national de la propriété industrielle) via the Guichet unique, onward to the Greffe du tribunal de commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of €50.10 per Ministerial Order implementing Article A123-22 of the Code de commerce

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory publication of the company formation notice (avis de constitution) in a legal-announcement journal (Journal d'annonces légales - JAL) of the registered-office department
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized French legal-announcement newspaper (JAL approved by the Préfet / Greffe)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated market benchmark (€160-€250 per notice); obligatory under Articles L123-12 and R123-5 of the Code de commerce

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional drafting of the Articles of Association (Statuts) for a multi-UBO SARL with non-resident shareholders, by a French corporate counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard SARL constituted by private deed (sous seing privé); no statutory tariff; notarial intervention optional absent an in-kind real-estate contribution

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and/or consular legalization processing bundle for UBO and manager documents (bundle of up to 4 original documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of each country of origin or French consular post
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official per-document fee of the issuing authority plus courier/handling; no single national tariff (Hague Convention 1961, French ratification of 24 January 1965)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of apostilled foreign documents (traduction assermentée; average 6-8 pages)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court-certified translator (traducteur assermenté près la cour d'appel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Approved page-based tariff applied by the cour d'appel listing (approx. €35-€55 per page)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: KYC/AML and sanctions clearance (UBO verification, PEP and adverse media checks, OFAC / UN / EU consolidated list screening, FATF country risk protocol)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance service provider / instructed law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per prospective client (individual check €40-€80; bundled rate for up to 3 natural persons)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year commercial domiciliation of the registered office (siège social) with a licensed domiciliation company
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Société de domiciliation agréée by the Préfet, or licensed PEX provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory framework under Commercial Code Articles R123-167 to R123-173; prevailing market benchmark €250-€300 per year, including mail handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional corporate bank account opening (setup fee and initial compliance dossier for Swift TT / Wire Transfer rails)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French credit institution or licensed neobank (e.g., BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Qonto)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year statutory registers and corporate kit (register of decisions / shareholders' minutes, share transfer register, corporate seal)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Legal stationer / law firm service desk

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial emoluments (tarif des notaires of the 1978 decree), approx. €400-€600 for a SARL constitution where the notary is retained

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), articles L. 223-1 et seq. (Sociétés à responsabilité limitée)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Dépôt des statuts de la SARL au greffe du tribunal de commerce
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required; minimum €1 with full subscription and payment in cash, no escrow account mandated
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company subscribe to the entire initial share capital of one thousand Euros (€1,000), represented by one thousand (1,000) shares of one Euro (€1) par value each, all subscribed and fully paid up in cash by the incorporators. The registered office is established at [Insert full address], France. The Board appoints [Director 1 Name] as Chairman and [Manager Name] as Managing Director (Gérant). The Managing Director is granted full powers to represent the Company in all acts of management, including opening bank accounts and signing contracts. This resolution is adopted unanimously in accordance with the Articles of Association and French law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Signing, and Notarization of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public and Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare detailed articles of association including share capital, object of the company, directors, manager, and registered office. Sign before a notary for authentication. Obtain certified copies.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity and share subscription of incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, provide additional documents or request a procedural extension from the greffe.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission and Registration of Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via guichet-entreprises.fr or in-person at the registry office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized articles of association along with proof of capital payment and other mandatory documents through the official online portal or at the counter. Obtain the SIREN number and extract Kbis upon approval.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of directors and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any formal defects by submitting corrected documents within the allowed period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: N/A - No specific industrial licensing required for wholesale trade activities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique et de la Cohésion des territoires
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A - No production or manufacturing processes; no wastewater, VOCs, or waste handling from industrial activities

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: General compliance with fire safety regulations and occupational health and safety standards; may require clearance from local fire department and labor inspection authorities depending on premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); official taxpayer portal: impots.gouv.fr (Espace Professionnel); business registration via the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The French SARL is incorporated through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises; INSEE issues the statutory SIREN (9-digit) and SIRET (14-digit) identifiers, after which DGFiP activates the tax file at the competent SIE and allocates the intra-Community VAT number (TVA intracommunautaire, format FR + 11 characters). Non-established foreign entities carrying out taxable French transactions must apply directly for French VAT registration at the SIE (CGI Art. 286) and, when established outside the EU, generally must appoint a DGFiP-accredited fiscal representative (CGI Art. 289 A) for VAT filings and refunds.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the SARL is subject by default to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) on its worldwide taxable profits; the standard IS rate in mainland France is 25%, and an additional 3.3% social solidarity contribution applies to IS exceeding EUR 763,000 for high-turnover companies. The SARL is not tax-transparent by default and is scoped according to permanent-establishment and treaty territorial rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no check-the-box regime. Under CGI Art. 239 bis AA, a qualifying closely held SARL owned by natural persons may elect the pass-through/partnership tax status (régime fiscal des sociétés de personnes, taxed at impôt sur le revenu) for a renewable five-fiscal-year period; the election is filed with the corporate income tax return and binds all members. Elective group relief is available through the parent-subsidiary regime (régime mère-fille) and tax consolidation (intégration fiscale), while ATAD hybrid mismatch rules apply mandatorily without elective alignment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) - French Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 for established taxable persons; a French SARL effecting taxable matcha-trading supplies must be VAT-registered from the first euro of taxable turnover (CGI Arts. 256 and 286). For non-established sellers, the annual EUR 10,000 EU-wide distance-sales threshold applies to intra-Community B2C distance sales; the existence of a French warehouse, fulfilment centre, or permanent establishment removes the threshold and triggers compulsory French VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Phased mandatory structured e-invoicing for all domestic B2B transactions through an accredited Dématérialisation Partenaire platform (PDP) or the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF), using standard formats Factur-X, UBL, or CII, with electronic signature/sealing and archiving obligations: from 1 September 2026 all French-established taxable persons must be able to receive e-invoices and large/mid-size taxpayers must issue them; from 1 September 2027 small and micro taxpayers must also issue them. Cross-border B2B and B2C transaction data are submitted by e-reporting to DGFiP through the same transmission channels; no SDI-style real-time pre-approval is currently required, but platform custody and clean-data invoice numbering apply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Matcha powder physically dispatched or transported to a destination outside the EU is exempt from French VAT (zero-rated) when the seller establishes that the goods left EU customs territory within 90 days of the supply by documentary evidence (CGI Art. 262-I; BOI-TVA-CHAMP-30-20). Intra-Community supplies to an EU VAT-identified customer are exempt where the customer's valid intra-Community VAT number is quoted on the invoice and the recapitulative statement/EC Sales List is filed. International B2B auxiliary services (freight, insurance, inspection, store-keeping) supplied to a customer established outside the EU are outside French VAT by the place-of-supply rule (CGI Art. 259), and input VAT attributable to zero-rated export sales remains deductible.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic export declaration lodged through the French Single Window/DELTA customs system)
Bill of Lading (connaissement) or equivalent transport document (sea waybill, air waybill, CMR consignment note) proving physical dispatch outside the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate: SWIFT MT103 credit advice or bank statement evidencing receipt of the foreign sales proceeds from the overseas buyer
Commercial export invoice, order documentation, and certificate of origin or health/certification papers for organic ceremonial-grade matcha
Intra-Community recapitulative declaration (Déclaration d'Échanges de Biens and EC Sales List) for goods delivered to VAT-registered customers in other EU member states
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP reconciles export zero-ratings against customs exit data and banking flows; missing, inconsistent, or late export documentation triggers reinstatement of French output VAT, disallowance of related input VAT, 0.20%-per-month statutory late interest (CGI Art. 1727), and penalties of 40% or 80% for bad-faith misdeclaration, fraud, or obstruction (CGI Arts. 1729 and 1732). Circular or staged export arrangements, false certificates of shipment, and systematic non-repatriation of proceeds may additionally trigger criminal tax-fraud proceedings (CGI Art. 1741), customs seizure, joint personal liability of the SARL gérant, and exclusion from simplified legalization and export-refund procedures.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, operating within the Eurosystem under the monetary authority of the European Central Bank; prudential and anti-money-laundering supervision is also performed by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution and relevant European Union authorities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro, which is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. There is no general French foreign-exchange approval, capital-control registration, mandatory repatriation requirement, or profit-conversion restriction for a French SARL. Dividends, interest, royalties, shareholder-loan repayments, and trade payments may generally be remitted abroad through regulated payment institutions, subject to corporate-law solvency and distributable-profit rules, withholding-tax requirements, transfer-pricing documentation, sanctions screening, beneficial-owner verification, and bank evidence of the underlying transaction. EU sanctions, anti-money-laundering rules, tax reporting, customs controls, and possible foreign-investment or national-security screening may still restrict particular counterparties or transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, mandatory conversion ratio, or universal deadline for converting or repatriating export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained in euros or foreign currency and credited to accounts in France or elsewhere, subject to bank due diligence, accounting records, customs evidence, sanctions controls, and applicable tax reporting. The company should retain commercial invoices, transport and customs records, contracts, payment confirmations, and reconciliation records sufficient to establish the economic purpose and source of funds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Groupe BPCE, including Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Epargne networks

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for operational payments, foreign-currency collections, expense management, and SEPA transfers where the provider is licensed as an EU electronic-money institution or payment institution and passported or otherwise authorised to serve France. An offshore digital EMI without EU authorisation, passporting, a regulated correspondent, or satisfactory French customer due diligence is not a reliable substitute for a French bank account and may be unable to hold client funds, provide a French IBAN, process regulated payment services, or support capital escrow. Fintech accounts should not be used for statutory capital deposits unless the provider and the receiving notary or bank expressly confirm legal acceptance. The SARL remains responsible for sanctions screening, AML controls, accounting evidence, VAT and customs reconciliation, and payment-service-provider limits.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch for corporate account opening. Remote onboarding and video identification may be available, particularly for EU-resident directors and straightforward ownership structures. The bank may nevertheless require an in-person meeting, notarised or apostilled documents, certified translations, live video interviews, original-signature verification, or attendance at a French branch based on risk, non-resident ownership, complex control chains, high transaction volumes, high-risk jurisdictions, or inability to complete electronic identification. The statutory representative, beneficial owners, authorised signatories, and persons controlling the account must be fully identified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or inconsistent corporate identity information, including mismatch between the articles, Kbis extract, beneficial-owner register, bank application, and ownership chart.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent Kbis extract; certified articles of association; registration and tax identifiers; current beneficial-owner declaration; ownership and control chart to natural persons; directors' resolutions; specimen signatures; valid identification and address evidence for directors, signatories, and beneficial owners; written explanation of any discrepancy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership, nominee arrangements, trusts, layered holding companies, or inability to identify the ultimate natural-person beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete group structure chart; incorporation and good-standing documents for each intermediary entity; shareholder registers; certificates of incumbency; beneficial-owner declarations; trust or nominee documentation where applicable; source-of-wealth statements; source-of-funds evidence; legal ownership and control analysis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of capital, shareholder loans, intercompany funding, or large incoming transfers inconsistent with the stated business profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital-increase or shareholder-loan documents; shareholder and board approvals; bank statements; audited or management accounts; investment-fund evidence; tax returns where requested; transfer-pricing or financing rationale; remitter-to-beneficial-owner reconciliation; payment purpose and capital-account instructions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Matcha suppliers, customers, logistics providers, or payment counterparties located in sanctioned, embargoed, or high-risk jurisdictions, or use of opaque intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty KYC files; sanctions-screening results; supplier and customer contracts; beneficial-owner attestations; country-risk assessment; import and export documentation; bills of lading; certificates of origin; customs declarations; end-use and end-user statements; documented escalation and approval records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction activity inconsistent with the declared business, including rapid pass-through funds, cash-intensive activity, unrelated cryptocurrency flows, unusual third-party payments, or excessive high-value transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury policy; twelve-month transaction forecast; supplier and customer concentration analysis; purchase orders; invoices; inventory and warehouse records; customs and transport documents; expected payment-flow diagram; reconciliation controls; explanation for third-party payments; management accounts demonstrating commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Organic or food-product trade documentation does not support the declared import and distribution activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier contracts; commercial invoices; purchase orders; certificates of organic compliance where applicable; product specifications; lot and traceability records; customs entries; freight and insurance documents; warehouse agreements; customer distribution contracts; VAT and accounting registrations; evidence that payments correspond to genuine goods movement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed person status, adverse media, criminal allegations, regulatory enforcement, or unexplained wealth involving a director, beneficial owner, supplier, or customer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP disclosure; enhanced due-diligence questionnaire; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; independent corporate and litigation searches; tax and financial records; compliance officer assessment; documented senior-management approval; ongoing monitoring and periodic review plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure to provide reliable tax residence, VAT, customs, or beneficial-owner information, or refusal to disclose the economic purpose of payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French tax and VAT registrations where applicable; tax-residence certificates; customs EORI information; UBO declarations; annual accounts or opening balance sheet; business plan; expected jurisdictions and currencies; written transaction-purpose memorandum; authorised-contact details for ongoing compliance requests.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a new SARL, route subscribed capital to a French bank's blocked capital escrow account or another institution legally accepted by the receiving notary or registration process. Use a transfer from the shareholder's own verified account, with the beneficiary name matching the SARL or the designated capital-deposit arrangement. State the transfer purpose as paid-in share capital or capital increase, identify the shareholder and subscription documents, and avoid unexplained third-party remitters. Provide the bank with the signed articles, subscription or capital-increase resolution, shareholder register, ownership chart, Kbis or formation file, beneficial-owner information, identification documents, and source-of-funds evidence. After incorporation or registration, obtain the deposit certificate and request release to the operating account. For subsequent shareholder loans or equity injections, use a separate documented purpose, executed loan or subscription agreement, board or shareholder approval where required, and accounting classification. Incoming EUR payments should preferably use SEPA Credit Transfer; non-EUR or non-SEPA payments should use SWIFT with complete originator, beneficiary, intermediary-bank, purpose, and fee instructions. Reconcile each receipt to the general ledger and retain the wire confirmation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments to eligible European suppliers and customers, with verified IBAN and beneficiary-name controls. Use SWIFT MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments, with complete ordering-customer, beneficiary, intermediary-bank, invoice, and purpose information. Use documentary commercial letters of credit, preferably confirmed where counterparty or country risk justifies confirmation, for new or higher-risk suppliers; define documentary conditions precisely, including commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, certificate of origin, organic certificate where contractually required, insurance document, inspection evidence, and customs-related records. Use documentary collections only where the risk profile is acceptable. Apply dual approval, segregation of duties, sanctions screening, invoice and purchase-order matching, supplier bank-account callback verification, and three-way reconciliation. Do not use personal accounts, anonymous payment instruments, unlicensed money-service businesses, or third-party settlement accounts. Retain invoices, customs documents, proof of delivery, freight records, payment messages, and reconciliation evidence for the applicable French accounting, tax, AML, and customs retention periods.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/foreign-currency forwards with an EU-authorised bank or regulated investment firm, supported by documented forecast trade exposures and within approved counterparty limits.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies subject to local convertibility or settlement restrictions, provided the counterparty is regulated, the contract is documented under an appropriate master agreement, and the settlement and reporting treatment is understood.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for documented funding or liquidity exposures, subject to board-approved risk limits, collateral terms, counterparty credit assessment, and appropriate accounting treatment.

Plain-vanilla currency options and participating forwards for proportionate hedging of committed or highly probable trade exposures, subject to suitability review, premium controls, and prohibition on speculative activity.
Natural hedging through matching currency receipts and payments, currency-denominated supplier contracts, settlement-netting arrangements, and maintenance of controlled currency liquidity buffers.

All derivatives should be executed with regulated counterparties under documented treasury policies, ISDA or equivalent contractual terms where appropriate, confirmations, valuation and collateral procedures, exposure monitoring, management approvals, and transaction records. Hedging must be consistent with applicable European Market Infrastructure Regulation, bank suitability requirements, accounting standards, sanctions controls, and the company's stated commercial exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual financial statements at the Ordinary General Meeting of shareholders (AGO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate organ; signed minutes retained in the statutory minute book at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after fiscal year end; commercial court may grant an extension upon request of the managing director
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: EUR 4,500 fine imposed on the legal representative for failure to convene the meeting in time; any shareholder may petition the commercial court to order the meeting be called

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of audited/approved annual accounts and management report with the Commercial Registry (Depot des comptes annuels et du rapport de gestion)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, filed electronically through the Guichet Unique national business registration portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of AGO approval and in all cases no later than 7 months after fiscal year end for electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: EUR 183 late-filing fine for the first month plus EUR 45 per additional month; judicial injunction with coercive daily penalty; prolonged default impairs Siren credit rating and exposes the entity to forced strike-off from the trade register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Liasse fiscale, Form 2065 and mandatory schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFIP Direction Generale des Finances Publiques, submitted by EDI-TDFC electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year ending 31 December: April 30, extended to May 3 for electronic filing; staggered fiscal year ends: within 3 months of the fiscal year closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-filing surcharge (5% if regularized within 30 days of formal notice) plus late-payment interest of 0.2% per month of the underlying tax; deliberate non-filing attracts 40% fraud penalty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of Beneficial Ownership Register data (Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the Guichet Unique portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Confirmed together with the annual accounts deposit (7-month cap after fiscal year end); any change in ultimate beneficial ownership must additionally be declared within 15 days of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under Article L.561-7 of the Monetary and Financial Code: up to 6 months imprisonment and EUR 7,500 fine for natural persons, EUR 37,500 fine for legal entities for omission or false beneficial-ownership declarations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual settlement of the property-based business tax (Cotisation Fonciere des Entreprises, CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFIP local tax collection offices for the commune of the registered establishment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Single annual payment due December 15 of the assessment year; assessment is automatic and based on the prior-year declared installation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge plus 1.2% quarterly late interest; enforced recovery through bank attachment may follow; no administrative strike-off exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statement of commissions and fees paid to commercial agents and intermediaries (DAS2)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFIP corporate income tax center (Service des Impots des Entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing by January 31 following the calendar year of payment; extended to February 15 for electronic submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: EUR 50 penalty per missing declaration, capped at EUR 150, plus EUR 20 per omitted or incorrect beneficiary record, capped at EUR 100; deliberate concealment triggers a 25% surcharge on amounts not declared

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) for SARL when exceeding at least two of three thresholds: balance-sheet assets above EUR 4,000,000; turnover excluding VAT above EUR 8,000,000; average workforce above 50 employees; also mandatory for holding companies controlling at least one subsidiary and for entities subject to consolidated supervision
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP per the Plan Comptable General, ANC Regulation 2014-03 as amended; IFRS is permitted only for consolidated group financial statements or listed parent companies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every share transfer, new subscription, or indirect ownership restructure affecting control must be recorded in the share-transfer ledger and reflected in the Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs within 15 days of the operation; the registry database is re-confirmed yearly when annual accounts are deposited through the Guichet Unique, and the managing director must certify continued accuracy of all beneficial-ownership data as part of the annual filing cycle
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of share transfers and movements (Registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of shareholders' meeting minutes and written unanimous decisions (Registre des proces-verbaux des assemblees generales)
Register of managing director's decisions and delegations (Registre des decisions de gerance)
Register of beneficial owners (Registre des beneficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $1,300 - $4,000 per year for accredited business domiciliation services in France, with Paris and Ile-de-France at the top of the range
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $4,000 - $10,000 per year for an abbreviated voluntary audit engagement; full statutory certification by a registered statutory auditor for a mid-size SARL ranges from $8,000 to $18,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard French corporate income tax rate applicable for fiscal years commencing on or after 1 January 2022; transitional rates of 26.5% for 2021 and 28% for 2020 do not apply to a newly established SARL in the current filing cycle unless grandfathering arises).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on the first €42,500 of taxable profit per fiscal year for qualifying small and medium-sized enterprises (turnover below €10 million, paid-up capital not exceeding €750,000, at least 75% of capital held by individuals or qualifying SME entities). Additional effective-rate reliefs: research tax credit (Créance d'Impôt Recherche) at 30% up to €100 million of qualifying expenditure; innovation tax credit (Créance d'Impôt Innovation) for SMEs; young innovative enterprise exemption; and deduction of 30% for certain trademark and patent licence fees where substance conditions are met. The matcha distribution activity is a standard commercial trade and will ordinarily fall within the 15% reduced band only if the statutory SME conditions are satisfied, otherwise the 25% headline rate applies on the whole taxable profit.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No statutory time limit (indefinite carryforward) under French law; however, annual utilisation is capped at €1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding €1,000,000 in the offset year. A one-year carryback (crédit d'impôt pour déficit reporté en arrière) is available up to €1,000,000 subject to distribution and solvency conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (Cerfa No. 15946) 'Déclaration de résultats et des éléments taxables' together with the standardized tax annexes (liasse fiscale: Forms 2052-SD through 2059-SD), filed electronically through the Impots.gouv.fr professional portal (Espace Professionnel / EDI-TDFC or EFI platform). For SARLs subject to corporate income tax, the majority of operating companies also file Form 2065-B (simplified tax computation) when eligible for the simplified scheme.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December: the return must be filed by 3 May of the following year; an extended deadline of 15 May applies when the return is filed electronically via the authorised EDI/EFI channel. For any fiscal year ending on another date: the deadline is the end of the third month following the close of the fiscal year. A supplementary declaration of items and tax credits (for example, Form 2069-A for the R&D credit) is due within the same statutory period; the balance of corporate income tax is payable electronically on the 15th day of the month following the filing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Résultat net comptable (net accounting profit before corporate income tax).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL must convert all revenues and costs into EUR in accordance with tax accounting rules; non-resident shareholders holding the SARL must ensure that the legal entity's stand-alone statutory accounts are used, not a consolidated or home-office adjusted figure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bénéfice fiscal (taxable income after judicial and extra-accounting restitution adjustments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlled SARLs must include all attributable French-source trading income; any transfer-pricing correction under Article 57 of the French General Tax Code must be reflected here; the same figure is the starting point for the 25% taxation or the SME 15% reduced band.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Déficit fiscal (tax loss available for carryforward).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only an SARL maintaining a genuine permanent establishment in France may recognise a French tax loss; non-resident investors cannot repatriate or offset this loss against their domestic income unless a treaty expressly permits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2065 – Cadre D, Line 3525 / Computation Block
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impôt sur les sociétés computed at the applicable rate (25% standard; 15% reduced rate on the initial €42,500 tranche for qualifying SMEs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The computed corporate income tax must be paid by direct debit or electronic transfer; monthly instalments (acomptes) already paid by the SARL are credited against this line and any balance must clear the treasury account before the statutory deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and withholdings: French withholding tax credits, foreign tax credits, the research tax credit (CIR) and the innovation tax credit (CII).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent company may not use French tax credits unless the credit arises from French-source income effectively taxed in the hands of the SARL; a refund claim for excess credits requires the filing of Form 2065-SD with the competent French tax centre and, where a treaty is invoked, a valid certificate of residence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing triggers an automatic 10% increase of the net corporate tax due (Article 1728 of the French General Tax Code); where the return is filed within thirty days of a formal notification, the penalty increases to 40%; where the return is deliberately irregular, 80% plus daily late interest at 0.20% per month. A fixed penalty of €150 (per annex schedule) applies for each missing supporting statement. Criminal prosecution under Article 1741 CGI is possible where the omission is intentional, exposing the SARL to a €500,000 fine and the managing director to five years' imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory withholding tax on dividends distributed by a French SARL to a non-resident corporate shareholder (Article 119 bis and 243 bis CGI); where the shareholder is an individual, the flat levy of 12.8% plus 17.2% social levies applies (total 30%) unless treaty relief is established.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced dividend withholding rate, the non-resident corporate shareholder must obtain and file a formal certificate of tax residence (for legal entities, Form 5001 'Certificat de résidence') with the French paying company before the distribution date; the certificate must be validated by the foreign tax authority and must indicate the applicable treaty article. Where the parent is established in the EU/EEA and holds at least 5% of the SARL for an uninterrupted period of two years, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (90/435/EEC) exemption is available without prior administrative approval, subject to anti-abuse and substance checks. For jurisdictions without a validated certificate, the paying company must apply the statutory 25% withholding; reimbursement can subsequently be claimed by the shareholder through the French tax authority's refund procedure (réclamation contentieuse) within the statutory limitation period, supported by the original certificate and proof of actual beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding tax of 33.33% on patent, know-how and trademark royalties paid by a French debtor to a non-resident (Article 182 B CGI); most comprehensive double tax treaties reduce this to 0% (e.g. EU Interest and Royalties Directive) or 5% (e.g. France-United States treaty), subject to submission of Form 5001 and satisfaction of the beneficial ownership clause. Interest: conventional arm's-length loan interest paid by a French SARL to a non-resident lender is generally exempt from French statutory withholding tax, provided the debt is not equity-disguised and no anti-abuse rule applies; however, interest remitted to a listed Non-Cooperative Jurisdiction (Etat non coopératif) is subject to a 75% withholding tax, and certain participating interest clauses attract a 25% or 50% levy; treaty reductions apply only where the recipient is the economic owner of the receivable.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File under Article L. 13 AA of the French Book of Tax Procedures apply when the French SARL (together with associated French enterprises) has annual gross turnover or total balance sheet assets of at least €400,000,000. Separately, when the ultimate parent group's consolidated turnover reaches €750,000,000, the French entity is obliged to file a Country-by-Country report (Form 2258-SD) and retain the Master File and Local File. Below these thresholds, there is no automatic annual filing obligation, but the French tax administration may serve a formal request (jeu de documents) during an audit and the taxpayer has 30 days to produce all transactional benchmark documentation. In practice, an SARL engaged in cross-border matcha procurement and distribution should maintain contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation wherever controlled transactions with the Japanese or other non-resident parent/affiliates exceed €1,000,000 in aggregate, and must be able to demonstrate an arm's-length margin for its distribution function.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) analogous to the UAE or other offshore jurisdictions; however, the concept of real economic substance is embedded in French anti-abuse jurisprudence, the principal purpose test of Article 29 of the OECD Model, and the abuse-of-law doctrine (Article L. 64 of the French Book of Tax Procedures). A matcha powder distribution SARL must demonstrably maintain a physical French office or warehouse, employ personnel with decision-making authority in France, keep complete local accounting records, and execute procurement, logistics, inventory and sales functions locally. If the French SARL operates as a letterbox company without substance, the French tax authorities may re-characterise the interposed arrangements, deny treaty benefits, and impose the 80% penalty for abusive tax arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of e-commerce and wholesale matcha revenues from Form 2065-SD, concealment of bank accounts abroad, or invoicing a portion of the margin through a shell entity in a low-tax jurisdiction without any commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax penalties: 40% surcharge for serious misstatement (Article 1729 CGI) or 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres, plus 0.20% monthly late interest. Criminal penalties under Article 1741 CGI: imprisonment of the managing director for up to five years, fine of up to €500,000 for the legal entity, and publication of the judgment at the convicted party's expense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil is available under Article L. 223-22 of the French Commercial Code and the 'action en comblement du passif' doctrine: directors who committed faults causing the tax debt may be judicially ordered to satisfy the SARL's tax liabilities personally; travel bans (interdiction de sortie du territoire), prohibition of commercial management for fifteen years, seizure of personal assets, and imprisonment are all judicially available in aggravated tax evasion cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Law (Abus de Droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the French SARL without real substance interposed solely to obtain treaty benefits on Japanese matcha procurement, routing payments through Malta or Singapore without operative functions, or using a nominee shareholder arrangement to conceal the ultimate beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration may invoke Article L. 64 of the Book of Tax Procedures to nullify the artificial arrangement and re-tax the transaction as if it had not been interposed; the 80% abusive-arrangement penalty applies in addition to the corrected tax and interest; treaty relief is automatically withdrawn if the principal purpose is tax avoidance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly executed the sham are jointly and severally liable for restitution of the evaded tax, civil damages to minority shareholders, and may be barred from exercising managerial functions; criminal exposure arises where the scheme is aggravated by cross-border money laundering, leading to confiscation of assets and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing intercompany matcha purchases from the Japanese related supplier above arm's-length value, granting unreasonably long payment terms, or allocating the French distributor a thin margin while the foreign related party retains the residual profit; failing to file the Form 2258-SD CbC report when group turnover exceeds €750,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Correction under Article 57 CGI with re-computation of the French taxable basis; penalties of 40% (or 80% in case of deliberate fraudulent transfer pricing) plus late interest at 0.20% monthly; a formal documentation summons under Article L. 13 AA carries a €10,000 fine for non-compliance and per-request €15,000 for repeat failure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director may be civilly liable to compensate the SARL for the additional taxes, penalties and interest if the transfer-pricing policy was an abnormal management act (acte anormal de gestion); French courts have ordered personal restitution where the director knowingly signed artificial invoice flows; aggravated cases involving export to sanctions-affected jurisdictions additionally trigger travel restrictions and criminal charges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accelerating dividend distributions immediately before a change of residence of the shareholder to obtain a lower treaty withholding rate; declaring deductible interest to a related company while accumulating distributable reserves; or failing to report the beneficial ownership of the distributing entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of the reduced withholding tax rate, reassessment at 25% (legal entities), 30% (individuals) plus anti-abuse penalty of 80% under the purpose test; late-payment interest is charged on the restored amounts; specific French anti-avoidance provisions (Article 119 ter CGI for intra-EU loopholes) allow retroactive reclassification of the distribution as taxable dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorised the distribution knowing it was designed to exploit treaty provisions are jointly liable for the shortfall in withholding taxes; where the SARL is insolvent, the director's personal assets can be reached; criminal sanctions are possible where manifestly fraudulent declarations were made to the tax authorities in support of the reduced rate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file or knowingly falsifying the beneficial ownership declaration (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs) at the Registry of the Commercial Court within one month of incorporation or any change in the shareholder structure; operating the SARL bank account as a pass-through vehicle for undisclosed related-party funds; or accepting payments from clients in a non-cooperative jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines under the French Monetary and Financial Code of up to €7,500 for the legal entity and up to €30,000 for directors for each omitted declaration; freezing of bank accounts upon suspicion of money-laundering; a 75% withholding tax on income remitted to a non-cooperative jurisdiction combined with denial of deductibility; criminal prosecution for laundering proceeds of tax fraud carries a five-year prison sentence and €375,000 fine for the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director acts as the SARL's legal representative and must exercise gatekeeper duties; French courts can order the director to personally return illicitly transferred funds; combined AML-tax sanctions allow a travel ban, confiscation of corporate and personal assets, and a commercial ban of up to fifteen years for being the effective conduit of the unlawful arrangement.
